challenge.better_approach: I looked at a codemother verb that answers read_attempts, which learning_block's proof would ask over the CLI. Measured: no verb exists, and its only consumer would be a test, so the orchestrator ruled against it. Proving at the owner is smaller and puts the claim where it belongs.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That read_attempts reaches legacy_trace_path through learning_block's module global, so the Windows seam patch works. Measured: trace_lines calls legacy_trace_path by module-global name, and learning_block's own clause 4 relies on the same lookup.
challenge.prior_art: Clause 4 of ticket a9709b744bf5 is the current proof of the claim, at the wrong address. clearance's proofs/ holds 15 proofs and none names read_attempts (grep). The legacy_trace_path seam pattern for Windows is copied from that learning_block proof.
challenge.real_collision: None. The learning_block proof keeps its clause 4 until ticket b1cb65682f26 narrows it, and that lands after this one, so the claim is never unproved.

answers.falsifier: Over a legacy-only store and a new-name-only store read_attempts returns the same 2 attempts and 1 unreadable line; with both present the legacy file's attempts come first. A reader that opens only the new-name file by hand reds both teeth.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ruled the shape 2026-11-16 after the measurement that no `cairn codemother` verb answers read_attempts: clause 4 of cairn/machines/learning_block/proofs/test_a_trace_file_name_is_legal_on_every_box.py imports cairn.devices.codemother.machines.clearance, and the claim moves to clearance's own address
answers.how: A proof under cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/proofs/ seeds the harbor_master:clearance block in a scratch CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT, once under the legacy name and once under the new name, and holds the same attempts and unreadable_lines from each, plus legacy-first order when both are present. No code changes.
answers.traces_to: RULE 1 (a proof measures only its own component) and Law 8 (nothing in proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): the clearance reader's either-store claim is CodeMother's, and today only a machine's proof that reaches into the device holds it.
answers.what: CodeMother's clearance proves at its own address that read_attempts counts the same over a legacy-named trace store and a new-name store, so the claim stays proved when learning_block stops measuring it.

bullets.text: The clearance reader's either-store count moves from learning_block's proof to clearance's own. A reader that opens only the new-name file by hand reds both teeth.
